repo_standards_ref: docs/agents/CREW_CONTEXT.md, docs/agents/GLOSSARY.md, references/global-crew.md, .agent-work/629-feature-view/g1-review/fowler_pass.json (sibling G1 precedent within the same package)

smells.finding: build_weekend_state_records's body (excluding docstring) is ~30 lines: two dict comprehensions, a has_session_type check, and one per-row for-loop with 3 short statements per axis. Not long by any repo precedent (sibling store.py methods are similarly short).
No classes defined -- module is a single free function plus a private helper (_none_if_nan).
No duplicated logic; _none_if_nan is written once and reused for both value and sigma normalization. No copy-pasted per-axis branches (the for-loop over model.axes covers all axes uniformly).
The only cross-object reach is into WeekendStateModel's own public accessors (model_cols(), layer_sigma_cols(), model.axes) -- exactly the sanctioned interface, not internals.
The (year, gp_name, session_type, constructor) tuple is read from each row and threaded into WeekendStateRecord's constructor.

override.repo_standard: Identical to G1's own already-logged override in .agent-work/629-feature-view/g1-review/fowler_pass.json citing src/physics/layer2/estimate_store.py's _PK tuple convention -- WeekendStateRecord (G1, frozen/closed this gate) already fixed this exact field shape; G2 merely populates a dataclass G1 already decided the shape of, not a new clump this gate introduces.
override.reason: Introducing a key value-object here would diverge from the sibling-store convention the plan already adopted at G1, for no behavior gain, and is out of this gate's authority to revisit (G1 is frozen/closed per the handoff's Specific Exclusions).

smells.finding: session_type/constructor/gp_name are read and passed through as raw str (str(row[...])).

override.repo_standard: Same standard G1 already logged: estimate_store.py/EstimateRecord's project-wide raw-str convention for these identity fields; GLOSSARY.md defines them as canonical string identities, not typed enums.
override.reason: Matching the established project-wide string-identity convention is required for interop with sibling stores/records this composer feeds; inventing a typed wrapper here would be a local divergence from a decision G1 already made and closed.

smells.finding: build_weekend_state_records takes 3 parameters (model, transformed_df, keyword-only model_version) -- well within any reasonable bound.
New, isolated composer; no existing call site needed edits (nothing yet imports build_weekend_state -- it is new, standalone production code awaiting G3-G5/its real caller).

The module has one reason to change: how a transformed-model row becomes a WeekendStateRecord. Column enumeration, the resolved/unresolved rule, and NaN normalization are all facets of that single responsibility, not independent axes of change.
No a.b.c.d chains. model.model_cols()/model.layer_sigma_cols() are single-level calls on the passed-in model; row.get(...) is a single dict lookup.

No unused hooks, reserved parameters, or abstract base classes introduced. The module docstring explicitly declines to build a per-axis reference-magnitude table it does not have data for ('doing so here would be inventing a number not in scope') -- the opposite of speculative generality: a deliberately deferred capability, not built ahead of need.

The module docstring is long (~75 lines) but explains non-obvious rationale that is NOT recoverable from the code alone: why round_idx is dropped (cites the sibling estimate_store.py _PK precedent), why the resolved/unresolved rule is a new convention distinct from estimate_store_fields._axis_statuses, and the session_type default's provenance. The code itself (the loop body) is short and not obfuscated -- comments explain WHY, not compensate for unclear HOW.
